provenance: 2026-08-27 Hurricane-Lala recovery (hfm #10 third artifact). moc's gateway retried 'Failed to connect to RNS: Attempt to register an already registered destination.' for 8+ days. The FIRST attempt in the journal said the truth: OSError 'Could not read ratchet file contents' -- a 0-byte ratchet (power-loss truncation) made register_delivery_identity() raise AFTER the destination was registered with Transport, so every retry hit 'already registered' and the real cause scrolled away. The skill: on a repeating setup error, scroll the journal back to the FIRST occurrence after process start -- the steady-state error names the wrong cause.

input.question: the gateway logs 'Attempt to register an already registered destination' on every RNS reconnect attempt and never comes back -- what do I check first?

provenance: 2026-08-27. After the Lala power loss, 13 state files fleet-wide were 0-byte or NUL-filled (ext4 allocates the block, data never flushes): 12 LXMF *.ratchets across 4 boxes + 2 NUL lines in mini's history jsonl. Every consumer crashed at next start (lxmd, nomadnet, gateway) or read degraded forever (mini history_integrity). Cure is uniform: quarantine the corpse (rename, keep for forensics), restart the consumer, announce/re-derive. RNS's own Critical log prescribes removal.

input.question: after an unclean power loss a service crashloops at start with OSError or InsufficientDataException on one of its state files -- what is the likely cause and the cure?

provenance: 2026-08-27. The steady-state error mentions RNS and the box's diagnostic even printed 'Restart rnsd: sudo systemctl restart rnsd' -- the misleading cure the message invites. rnsd was healthy (Up, serving 5 programs, peers reachable); restarting it fleet-wide is the documented @rns-race hazard. The real cause was a corrupt ratchet crashing setup after partial registration; the cure is quarantine + gateway restart. A proposal to make 'restart rnsd' the standing cure for this signal must not be ratified.
